agents.name: Cabozantinib
agents.type: Targeted therapy: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Cabozantinib blocks several growth signals, including MET, AXL and VEGFR. These signals help cancer cells grow and form a blood supply. Blocking them can slow the cancer, but also affects normal blood vessels, skin, bowel and wound healing.
agents.explanation: Cabozantinib blocks several growth signals, including MET, AXL and VEGFR. These signals help cancer cells grow and form a blood supply. Blocking them can slow the cancer, but also affects normal blood vessels, skin, bowel and wound healing.
risks: High blood pressure, including hypertensive crisis; heart problems and arterial or venous clots
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, reduced appetite and weight loss
Painful palms and soles, rash, sore mouth, taste changes, fatigue and voice changes
Liver injury, thyroid changes and low calcium or other electrolyte disturbances
Protein in urine and occasionally nephrotic syndrome with swelling
Serious bleeding; bowel perforation or fistula, which may be fatal
Delayed wound healing and osteonecrosis of the jaw (jaw-bone damage)
Rare brain swelling syndrome (PRES), seizures or visual disturbance; blood-cell changes
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea and painful palms/soles early. Confirm your prescribed symptom medicines and blood-pressure plan. Tell the team before surgery or dental procedures: treatment usually needs withholding at least 28 days beforehand, with restart only after review of healing.

anatomy: Fatigue may reflect thyroid changes. Sudden severe headache, confusion, seizures or sight changes need emergency care.
Report mouth ulcers, jaw pain, loose teeth or a wound that will not heal. Tell your dentist about cabozantinib.
Check pressure as directed. Severe chest pain, breathlessness or stroke symptoms need emergency care.
Tests check liver function and body salts. Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or marked weakness needs prompt advice.
Diarrhoea can dehydrate you. Call for persistent symptoms; severe abdominal pain, black stools or vomiting blood is urgent.
Urine checks detect protein leakage. Report new swelling, foamy urine or reduced urine.
Painful or peeling palms and soles can affect walking. Report early and use the skin-care plan.
Report a painful swollen leg, unusual bleeding or unhealed wounds. Agree treatment interruptions before surgery or dental work.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Cabozantinib blocks several growth signals, including MET, AXL and VEGFR. These signals help cancer cells grow and form a blood supply. Blocking them can slow the cancer, but also affects normal blood vessels, skin, bowel and wound healing.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: METEOR compared cabozantinib with everolimus after VEGF-targeted therapy. The primary progression-free analysis in 375 patients showed medians of 7.4 versus 3.8 months (hazard ratio 0.58; 95% confidence interval 0.45–0.74). In the full 658-patient population, a subsequent overall-survival analysis showed 21.4 versus 16.5 months (hazard ratio 0.66; 95% confidence interval 0.53–0.83). These are group estimates from different analyses, not an individual prediction.

items.title: Fertility and contraception
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least four months afterwards; add a barrier method to hormonal contraception. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least four months afterwards.

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Discuss benefit, burden, alternatives including supportive care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment. Trial averages cannot predict your own outcome.
